Before wrapper reads actor hand stack once, sets shared cachedPriorityZeroResult to PASS. It searches active actor PreventEntityUsePower first, then target PreventBeingUsedPower. First applicable entry executes its actions and returns its factory-fixed FAIL immediately, bypassing remaining own phases and wrapped Entity.interact invocation. This is callback-local refusal, not proof final Player.interact result stays FAIL.

Both prevention powers check configured hands, nullable item predicate using holder world plus supplied actor stack, then nullable ordered actor/target pair predicate. Actor-owned pair is (holder,other); target-owned pair is (other,holder). Both execute bi-entity action first then actor item handling. Target-side prevention still mutates the interacting player hand. Powers are not all combined into an AND and the first successful actor-side predicate takes precedence over every target-side veto.

Non-veto path collects eligible actor and target active interaction powers with priority>=0 into shared buckets; actor query is added before target query. Predicates use the same initial stack reference before any bucket action runs. Each bucket is visited descending integer priority; every included power in a visited bucket executes even after an earlier action supplied an accepted result. Power availability/conditions are not rechecked during that bucket execution. A callback may mutate state or the stack; no rollback/snapshot isolation is supplied.

Bucket result starts PASS. For each action it chooses currentResult if current.isAccepted && !previous.isAccepted, else if current.shouldSwingHand && !previous.shouldSwingHand. This is the literal two-step fold, not simply highest-priority veto, last-result wins, or proof only the selected action executed. Do not infer native enum flag truth tables from names; exact ActionResult implementation not read.

For positive priorities, non-PASS folded result requests swing if shouldSwingHand then returns without wrapped native invocation. PASS bucket permits lower buckets. At priority0 the folded result is cached and the wrapper continues, ultimately calling original.call(instance,player,hand). Thus zero-priority actions may already have run even when native interaction subsequently executes. Priority0 is a dispatch phase, not another independent credited mechanism.
